title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority routing, burst controls, and utilization reporting (v2)
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves Dedicated autoscaler with priority-aware routing, smoother burst tokenbucket behavior, and enhanced per-fleet utilization reporting. Adds metrics and Grafana dashboards for operator visibility. Backwards-compatible config changes; no breaking changes.
body: Context: This PR addresses operational gaps we saw during recent Dedicated fleet saturation exercises (ENG-3142). It combines three related feature areas into a single rollout: 1) priority-aware routing for the dedicated autoscaler so high-priority customers get preserved burst capacity; 2) smoothing and deterministic behavior for the burst tokenbucket to avoid feedback oscillations under transient load; and 3) enhanced utilization reporting with per-fleet and per-priority bucketing for SLO-driven dashboards. Motivation: Customers running multi-tenant Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees and visible utilization so they can plan commitments and detect over-subscription. The previous autoscaler treated all traffic uniformly which led to suboptimal evictions of high-priority routes and noisy bursts that tripped scaling repeatedly. Summary of changes (high-level commits): - Implement priority-aware enqueue routing and token accounting (3 commits) - Add burst tokenbucket smoothing and backoff heuristics (2 commits) - Emit new metrics: dedicated.fleet.utilization, dedicated.fleet.burst_tokens, dedicated.route.priority_drop_count (4 commits) - Wireup Grafana dashboards and alert rules (1 commit) - Tests and integration harness updates (2 commits) Files changed (high-level): - pkg/autoscaler/router.go: add priority routing policy and unit tests - pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go: introduce smoothing window and deterministic refill - pkg/autoscaler/handler.go: maintain per-priority counters and expose metrics - observability/dashboards/dedicated_fleet_overview.json: new dashboard panels - docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md: document new config knobs and rollout guidance - test/integration/dedicated_autoscaler_test.go: new load tests and assertions Small code snippets (illustrative): - priority routing: router.Enqueue(req) now tags request with priority and updates reserved token accounting - tokenbucket smoothing: refill uses EWMA(window=30s) to avoid sudden refill spikes Review conversation (high-level): - Marco Ruiz (reviewer): "Can we ensure the new metrics are tagged with customer_id and region? Otherwise multi-region rollups will be noisy." Aisha: "Added customer_id and region tags where available; for legacy calls we fall back to 'unknown' so dashboards remain stable." - Leah Kim: "Nice work. Two nits: 1) document the safe rollout steps for Dedicated customers; 2) add a unit test for priority preemption edge case." Aisha: "Addressed both: docs updated and added test scenario that simulates priority preemption when capacity is 90%+." - Derek Shaw: approved with comment: "Make sure we monitor the tokenbucket smoothing latency impact on P95 decision path." CI and checks: - CI: unit tests passed (Go 1.21), integration tests ran in the perf-canary job, linting passed - Canary perf job: two runs against staging; minor transient increased scheduling latency on the first run that was resolved after tuning smoothing window - All checks green at merge time Merge outcome: merged via squash and merge on 2026-03-01 by Aisha Patel. Rollout plan: feature gated behind config flags: autoscaler.priority_routing.enabled and autoscaler.tokenbucket.smoothing.enabled. Default rollout: enable in staging for 48h, enable for 30% of clusters with high-priority customers for 7 days, then full rollout. Follow-ups and TODOs: - ENG-3410: add per-customer historical utilization export for billing pilot (follow-up PR) - Observe tokenbucket metrics during next 2 weeks to validate no regressions in tail latencies - Backfill dashboards in ops runbook and notify enterprise CS for customers with reserved capacity Notes: No breaking config changes; default behavior remains unchanged unless flags are enabled. The change reduces churn during burst events and improves capacity guarantees for high-priority routes.
